---
title: Typography
description: Headings, text, quotations, lists and callouts.
---

Tufte's books set the text in a single face, in a few sizes, with italic for
the headings and for emphasis. There is no bold heading and no coloured bar.
The hierarchy comes from size and space alone.

## A section heading

A second-level heading is in italic and in the normal weight. It has no rule
under it; the space above it is enough to start a new part of the page.

### A smaller heading

The third level is smaller, and still in italic. Below it the text goes on
in the same size as before, so that a reader moves from the heading to the
text with no change of voice.

## Text

A paragraph has a generous leading, about one and a half times the size of
the type. *Emphasis* is in italic, and **strong text** is in bold, which the
theme keeps for the rare word that must stand out. Numbers such as 1983 and
2006 use lining figures.

- A list keeps the size of the text.
- Its items have the same leading as a paragraph.
- A long item wraps under its own first word, not under the bullet, so that
  the column keeps a clean left edge.

> Above all else show the data. A quotation is set in from the left, with no
> rule beside it.

## Callouts

::: {.callout-note}
A note has a thin rule at its left in a muted blue, and no tinted box.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## A warning with a title
The title is in italic, the colour is a dark ochre.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
An important callout uses a deep red.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## A tip that folds
The body of a callout can fold away under its title.
:::
